transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Oceanic CTO), Evan Park (Eng Mgr), Lila Chen (Security)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough focused on rate limiting, quotas, and org/project key model. Customer is evaluating Redwood for multi-tenant inference across their telehealth apps; primary concerns are per-project isolation, burst handling, and audit logs for security/compliance. Decided to run a short POC with trial org/project keys and a benchmark of typical nightly batch jobs + user-facing chat flows.

Topics covered:
- Org vs project API keys and how they map to billing and quotas
- Rate limiting enforcement (token-based, per-route, burst windows)
- Console UI for quotas, alerts, and usage dashboards
- Multi-tenant controls, RBAC and audit logs (KMS, retention)
- POC plan and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Okay hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marta: Good, thanks. We wanted to focus mostly on rate limits and how org/project keys would work for our multi-tenant setup. We have a bunch of clinic partners sharing one account and we need separation.
[00:14] Priya: Totally — that's exactly what we're demoing today. We'll walk through the Console first to show org/project keys and quotas, then jump into the API behavior and some notes on enforcement and caching.
[00:25] Evan: Quick context — our current stack uses a mix of in-house endpoints plus a third-party LLM provider, and we've hit hard quota ceilings during peak scheduling windows. We're trying to understand tradeoffs: hosted API vs dedicated pools.
[00:36] Priya: Makes sense. Two quick clarifications — are you wanting per-clinic isolation for both billing and rate limits, or just rate-limits but shared billing?
[00:45] Marta: Ideally both, but billing can be aggregated initially. Security wants clear audit trails per clinic though.
[00:52] Lila: Yes, audit + retention, and we need KMS integration for key management, plus SSO for console access. SOC 2 is a must.
[01:00] Jordan: Great, those are all covered — we have org-level billing, and project keys can map to each clinic. You can set per-project quotas, and the Console has audit logs and KMS integrations. We'll show that in a sec, but quick note — Dedicated gives you stronger performance isolation if you need it.

[01:18] Priya: (screen share) Alright, Console home. Here you can see organization overview, usage for the month, and a Projects tab. I'm going to create a sample project called "Oceanic - Clinic A".
[01:30] Priya: When I create a project, Console issues a project API key. That key is scoped to the project and inherits org policies by default. In the Quotas section you can set a requests-per-minute limit, tokens-per-minute, and a monthly spend cap.
[01:43] Evan: So requests-per-minute can be per-route? Like limit chat generation separately from embeddings?
[01:49] Priya: Yep. You can define per-route quotas. For example, /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings can have separate caps. Also we support token-based quotas so heavy generation is throttled appropriately rather than just counting calls.
[02:01] Marta: How about burst handling? We have appointment loads that spike for 30-90 seconds after a patient action.
[02:07] Priya: Console supports a burst window — you can configure a short-term burst allowance above the steady-state RPS, and then a sustained quota. Our runtime also has smoothing so it tries to absorb microbursts via short buffering and adaptive batching.
[02:20] Jordan: Important to call out: for hosted plans, rate limits are enforced at the org/project layer in the control plane. For Dedicated, you can enforce limits locally on the pool for additional isolation and to avoid cross-tenant throttling.
[02:33] Lila: And audit logs — are request/response bodies stored? We need redaction controls.
[02:39] Priya: We store request metadata and token counts in the audit logs. By default we do not persist PII-containing responses unless you opt into longer retention; plus you can enable automatic redaction and use customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. We'll send the SOC 2/retention docs after the call.
[02:53] Evan: How do org/project keys look from the API? Is it just a header like Authorization: Bearer <key>?
[03:00] Priya: Exactly. Project keys are regular API keys scoped to a project. Org keys are higher privilege and can create projects, change quotas, etc. You can also create limited-service keys for internal services that only call embeddings endpoints.
[03:12] Jordan: We often see customers rotate keys automatically — Console has a rotate button and a short-lived token option for ephemeral use.

[03:23] Priya: Jumping to the Rate Limits page: here you can see active rules. I'm going to show an example rule — Project A: 500 requests/min, 2M tokens/day, route-level overrides for embeddings at 100 req/min.
[03:36] Priya: If you exceed a quota the API returns a 429 with a body that includes a standard error + the remaining retry-after header. The Console also can trigger alerts to Slack or PagerDuty when a project approaches its quota.
[03:48] Marta: Can we set different SLAs per clinic? Some of our partners have premium tiers.
[03:53] Priya: Yes — you can attach a tier to a project and the routing policy will favor premium capacity. You can have doorknobs for latency SLO-backed pools or cheaper best-effort pools.

[04:05] Evan: About multi-tenant controls — do you support tenant-level RBAC? For example, clinic admins should only see their project's usage.
[04:12] Priya: Yes RBAC is per-org with project-scoped roles. You can mint invite links for project-level admins which only show that project's dashboards.
[04:19] Lila: Is there an audit field with user email for each action? We need that for our compliance team.
[04:24] Jordan: Audit logs include actor identity (SSO user/email), action, timestamp, and resource. We'll include a sample audit log export.

[04:36] Priya: API demo time — I'll do a short curl against a project key. (typing) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer proj_live_abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","prompt":"hello"}'
[04:48] Priya: The response includes X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset headers. We also include token-usage metrics in the response meta for quick client-side accounting.
[05:00] Evan: Do you expose a consumption API for our billing system to pull daily usage per project?
[05:05] Priya: Yes, there's a Usage API endpoint and a CSV export in the Console for billing reconciliations.

[05:13] Marta: For the POC, we'd like 1) trial project keys; 2) sample usage export; 3) run a benchmark using our traffic shape. How long does provisioning take?
[05:22] Jordan: We can provision trial org+project keys today — Priya can create them now. For a dedicated pool POC it's usually a week to provision if you want reserved GPUs; hosted trials are immediate.

[05:33] Priya: Creating sample project now... (click) Done — project created: "Oceanic - POC Clinic". I've generated a project key, I'll paste it in the chat (note: demo key - not for production).
[05:45] Priya: Key rotation note: if you rotate the key, existing sessions will fail until swapped; we recommend short window staging for key rollover.

[05:55] Lila: On encryption — does KMS support Cloud KMS and customer HSM?
[05:59] Priya: Yes both. For private deployments we support on-prem HSM integration.

[06:05] Jordan: Let's talk throttling policies — you can choose hard limits that immediately reject, or soft-throttles that queue requests for a short period (useful for smoothing). Soft-throttle is configurable: max queue depth and max wait time.
[06:18] Evan: That queueing — does it add latency to user-facing chat?
[06:21] Priya: It can add a little tail latency if you let requests queue, but for sub-second waits it's often indistinguishable to users. For strict latency SLOs we recommend lowering batch windows and using dedicated pools to avoid queued waits.

[06:33] Marta: What about caching and prefix reuse? If multiple clinics are using similar prompts, can we cache to reduce tokens?
[06:39] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes prefix caching and reuse; Console surfaces cache hit rates and recommendations. Cache is per-project unless you opt into sharing across projects — which you'd typically avoid for tenant isolation.

[06:51] Jordan: A few real-world notes — customers often start on hosted, set conservative per-project quotas, and then if they need lower latency or higher throughput we help them migrate to Dedicated with the same org/project model.

[07:05] Evan: Side question — do you have rate limiting at the region level for geo-failover? If a region is overloaded can requests route to another region respecting org quotas?
[07:13] Priya: Yes we have smart routing policies. You can configure per-region fallback; quotas are evaluated at the logical org/project level and enforcement can be global or per-region depending on your policy.

[07:25] Marta: Ok good. For security review — can you share the SOC 2 report and a sample Data Processing Agreement?
[07:30] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll send the security pack.

[07:35] Priya: One thing to be aware of — when you use token-based quotas and batching, a single large batch may consume more tokens at once; so in quota settings set a token ceiling that accounts for your max batch size.
[07:47] Evan: Makes sense. We'll send our batch size distribution.

[07:52] Priya: I also wanted to demo alerts — you can set a threshold at 80% usage and have it trigger both email and Slack. (shows UI)
[08:00] Jordan: We also have programmatic webhooks that notify a webhook endpoint when a project hits threshold or is rate-limited.

[08:08] Marta: One last operational question — can we generate per-project keys that are read-only for usage metrics? We want to allow some partners to pull their usage without seeing console billing.
[08:16] Priya: Yep create a scoped API key with read:usage permission. It shows metrics only.

[08:23] Evan: Great — what's the recommended POC size? We can start small — one clinic with 2 weeks of production-like traffic.
[08:29] Priya: That works. For benching we'll instrument token metrics and tail latency. We'll also run a run-rate test to validate quotas and burst handling.

[08:38] Marta: Any gotchas?
[08:40] Jordan: Two things: account for max batch token usage when setting token quotas, and plan key rotation strategy for your services to avoid secret spill. Also if you plan to mix hosted + dedicated for failover, we'll show you how routing policies prefer dedicated pools but fallback to hosted under capacity constraints.

[08:55] Priya: I'm going to simulate hitting a quota — I'll ramp requests quickly to show a 429 and the Console alert. (runs script)
[09:05] Priya: And you can see the 429 body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Project quota exceeded","retry_after":30} — the Console just popped a warning and sent a Slack alert to the configured channel.

[09:20] Lila: Nice, that looks straightforward.

[09:23] Jordan: Alright let me recap next steps: Jordan will send pricing + security pack; Priya will provision trial org+project keys and set up a short benchmark plan; Marta will share traffic profile and SLOs. We'll aim for a POC kickoff the week of Jan 4.

[09:38] Marta: Sounds good. Any final Qs?
[09:41] Evan: Nope, thanks.
[09:42] Lila: Thanks everyone.
[09:43] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and keys.

(End of recording)

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription with a few mishearings — product names sometimes rendered as "Redwood Optimise" or "red wood" in the raw text. Some speaker labels adjusted post-export.
